subject: physics
question_text: When does a real gas behave like an ideal gas?

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2016 (Q9), March 2019 (Q9), March 2023 (Q3), March 2024 (Q9) and March 2025 (Q10) — five of the seven papers held, and the most-asked question in this corpus. Section A, 2 marks each time. The 2019 paper prints "When does real gas behave...", the same question with a dropped article. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question text itself is sourced from those papers. `appearances` is deliberately left empty — a separate reviewed tagging pass fills it, and a hand-written tag here would be an invented claim. Physics hand-checked against NCERT Class-11 Chapter 13: a real gas approaches ideal behaviour at low pressure and high temperature, where the intermolecular forces and the molecular volume are both negligible.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Name both conditions. One of the two alone does not earn it.
steps.why: The two conditions are the two ways of making the molecules far apart. Low pressure spreads them out in space, and high temperature gives them so much kinetic energy that the attraction between them changes their motion very little.
common_mistakes: Writing high pressure and low temperature. Those are the conditions under which a real gas differs MOST from an ideal gas.

recall.must_convey: That a real gas behaves like an ideal gas at low pressure and high temperature.
accept: at high temperature and low pressure

steps.memory_tip: Low pressure spreads the molecules out, high temperature keeps them moving. Far apart means ideal.

lines.text: Real gas → ideal: low P, high T

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Two reasons: no attraction between molecules, and no molecular volume.
steps.why: The ideal gas model makes exactly two assumptions — no force between molecules, and molecules of zero volume. Low pressure and high temperature are the conditions under which a real gas comes close to both of them.
common_mistakes: Giving only one reason. Two assumptions are dropped: the intermolecular force and the molecular volume.
Saying the molecules have no volume at all. Their volume is small against the volume of the container, not zero.

recall.must_convey: That the molecules are far apart, so the intermolecular forces and the molecular volume are both negligible.
accept: volume of the molecules is negligible

steps.memory_tip: Ideal means two things gone: the pull between molecules, and the molecules' own volume.
